chapters.title: Count with me
chapters.tagline: Touch each object once, then connect a small group to its number.
outcomes: I can count a small group.
I can match a group to a number.
I can find the next number.

vocab.meaning: Say one number for each thing you touch.
The last number you say tells how many.
The number that comes after.

see.title: Touch and count
text: Say a number for each touch.

see.title: The last number says how many
text: The last number you say is how many.

see.title: Match the group to its number
What comes next?
text: Hop one step to find the next number.

try.prompt: Show 3 counters. Tap the boxes and count.
try.hint: Tap one box at a time. Say the number each time. Stop at 3.
Count out loud as you tap. Stop when you say 5.

try.prompt: Which number comes after 6? Tap it.
try.hint: Find 6 first. The next number is one step on.

parents.idea: Your child learns to touch each thing once and say one number for each. The last number said tells how many. This is the base of all later number work.
parents.slip: Counting a thing twice or skipping one. Slide each object across as it is counted, so every one gets exactly one number.

tryAtHome.title: Count the snack
steps: Put up to 5 raisins or grapes on a plate.
Let your child touch and move each one while counting aloud.
Ask, "How many are there?" and listen for the last number.
Add one more. Ask what number comes next.

chapters.title: More, less and the same
chapters.tagline: Compare groups and everyday sizes without racing.
outcomes: I can find more or fewer objects.
I can compare big, tall and thick things.
I can compare weight and how full a jar is.

vocab.meaning: A bigger group. It has extra things.
A smaller group. It has less things.
Equal. Nothing is extra.
Hard to lift. The heavy side goes down.

see.title: Tall, short, thick, thin
text: This tower is tall. This one is short.
This book is thick. This one is thin.

c.caption: Tall and short. Thick and thin.

see.title: Heavy and light
text: When both are the same, the balance is level.

try.prompt: Make both sides the same. Add to the left side.
try.success: Yes! 2 and 3 more is 5. Both sides are the same.
try.hint: The right side has more. Add one at a time to the left until it is level.

try.prompt: Which are tall? Which are short? Sort them.
try.success: Yes! Tall things reach up. Short things stay low.
try.hint: Look at how high each one goes.

try.prompt: Which jar is full? Which is empty?
try.success: Yes! A full jar has no space left.
try.hint: Look for the jar with blue up to the top.

parents.idea: Your child compares groups by matching one to one, and compares size, weight and how full things are. The words more, fewer, tall and heavy come first.
parents.slip: Thinking the bigger-looking group has more. Line the objects up in two rows, one to one, so the extra ones show.

tryAtHome.title: Bath-time compare
steps: Fill two cups, one full and one nearly empty.
Ask, "Which is fuller? Which is empty?"
Line up 4 toys and 2 toys. Ask which row has more.
Pick two toys. Ask which one is heavier and why.

chapters.title: Meet the shapes
chapters.tagline: Name familiar outlines and notice corners and matching shapes.
outcomes: I can notice sides and corners.
I can find a shape in a picture.

vocab.meaning: A round shape with no corners.
4 straight sides the same. 4 corners.
3 straight sides. 3 corners.
A pointy place where two sides meet.

see.title: Circle, square, triangle
text: This is a circle. It is round.
This is a square. This is a triangle.

see.title: More shapes
text: A rectangle is a long square.
An oval is a long circle.
Here are a heart and a star too.

c.caption: Touch each corner as you count.

see.title: Shapes in a picture
text: The door is a rectangle. The window is a circle.

c.caption: Find the triangle, the rectangle and the circle.

try.prompt: Which shapes have corners? Which have none?
try.success: Yes! Square, triangle and rectangle have corners. Circle and oval do not.
try.hint: Run a finger around the edge. Do you feel a pointy corner?

try.prompt: Find the stars. Put the stars in the star box.
try.hint: A star has points. It looks like the star at the top of the box.

parents.idea: Your child learns to name the common shapes, match the same shape, and notice corners. Shapes are found everywhere in the home.
parents.slip: Calling a rectangle a square, or an oval a circle. Say that a rectangle is long and an oval is long and round.

tryAtHome.title: Shape hunt
steps: Walk around a room with your child.
Find something round (a plate), a square (a tile), a rectangle (a door).
Trace each shape with a finger. Count the corners.
Ask your child to point out one new shape.

chapters.title: Which ones belong?
chapters.tagline: Sort familiar things by one visible rule before combining clues.
outcomes: I can find things that belong together.
I can find the one that is different.
I can count just one group.

vocab.meaning: Put things that are alike in the same place.
Alike in one way, like colour.
Not like the others. The odd one out.

see.title: Sort by colour
text: The apple and the red block are red.
The ball and the blue block are blue.
We put red with red, blue with blue.

see.title: The odd one out
text: The star is different. It is the odd one out.

see.title: Count one group
text: Some counters are orange. Some are blue.

try.prompt: Put the red things in the red box. Put the blue things in the blue box.
try.success: Yes! Red with red and blue with blue.
try.hint: Look at the colour of each picture first.

try.prompt: Find the odd one out. Which one is different?
try.success: Yes! The fish is different from the apples.
try.hint: Three are the same. Which one is not?

parents.idea: Your child sorts things by one clear rule, such as colour, and finds the one that is different. Sorting is the start of data and logic.
parents.slip: Mixing two rules at once, like colour and shape. Pick one rule, say it aloud, then sort.

tryAtHome.title: Sock and toy sort
steps: Pile a few socks or toys on the floor.
Say one rule, like "Sort by colour".
Let your child make the groups. Ask, "Which group has more?"
Hide one odd item in a group. Ask your child to find it.

chapters.title: Where is it?
chapters.tagline: Use position words with toys, pictures and simple rows.
outcomes: I can find what is inside or outside.
I can find what is above or below.
I can find a place in a row.

vocab.meaning: Inside something, like a ball in a bowl.
Outside something, not inside it.
Higher up. Over something.
Lower down. Under something.

see.title: In and out
text: The ball is in the bowl.
The ball is out of the bowl.

see.title: Above and below
text: The ball is above the box.
The ball is below the table.

see.title: A place in a row
text: Count the toys from the left.
Ball is 1st. Apple is 2nd. Star is 3rd.

see.title: Third in the row
text: The star is 3rd in the row.

try.prompt: Which ball is in the bowl? Which is out?
try.success: Yes! One ball is in. One ball is out.
try.hint: Look at where the ball is. Is the bowl around it?

try.prompt: Which ball is above? Which ball is below?
try.success: Yes! Above is up high. Below is down low.
try.hint: Is the ball up high or down low?

try.prompt: The row is ball, apple, star, heart, fish. Tap the place of the heart.
try.hint: Count from the left: ball 1, apple 2, star 3, then the heart.

parents.idea: Your child uses words like in, out, above, below, first and last. These words build the base for maps, graphs and later geometry.
parents.slip: Mixing up above and below, or in and on. Use real objects: put a toy in a box, on a box, under a box.

tryAtHome.title: Teddy says
steps: Sit with a teddy and a box.
Say, "Put teddy in the box." Then "on", "under", "next to".
Line up 4 toys. Ask who is first and who is last.
Swap: let your child give the instructions to you.

chapters.title: What comes next?
chapters.tagline: Say the repeating group aloud and continue a picture pattern.
outcomes: I can continue a picture pattern.
I can find a missing picture.
I can notice how a pattern grows.

vocab.meaning: Pictures that repeat again and again.
The one that comes after.
The one that is not there. Find it.

see.title: Say it and repeat
text: Say it out loud as you point.

see.title: Find the missing picture
text: Say the pattern: fish, ball, fish, ball.
The hidden one is a ball.

try.prompt: Say the pattern. Pick the picture that comes next.
try.success: Yes! Star, heart, star, heart, star, heart.
try.hint: Say it from the start: star, heart, star, heart, star, ...

try.prompt: Two balls, then an apple. What comes next?
try.hint: The group is ball, ball, apple. We have ball, ball. Which one finishes it?

try.prompt: Find the missing picture in the middle.
try.success: Yes! Fish, ball, fish, ball, fish, ball.
try.hint: Say it again from the start. What comes before the ball?

parents.idea: Your child sees that some things repeat in a group, says the group aloud, and finds what comes next. Patterns are the first step to algebra.
parents.slip: Guessing without saying the whole group. Always say the pattern from the start, then point at each picture.

tryAtHome.title: Beads and blocks
steps: Line up red and blue blocks: red, blue, red, blue.
Ask your child to say it and add the next block.
Try a new group like red, red, blue.
Hide one block and ask which colour is missing.
